name: Bane
label: Equal Vision Records
lede: Aaron Dalbec was still a Converge guitarist when he started the band in Worcester that became Bane. It made four albums for Equal Vision, called Don't Wait Up its last in 2014, played a final show in Worcester in 2016, and came back for Stu Maguire in 2021 and for Boston in 2023.

eras.title: Worcester, on the side
eras.text: Aaron Dalbec started Gateway in 1994 while still playing in Converge. By 1995 Aaron Bedard had the microphone and the band had a new name, and for the next two years it played central Massachusetts and put out two EPs on Life Records.

years.h: A Converge guitarist starts a side band called Gateway
years.p: Aaron Dalbec and Damon Bellorado start it in Worcester, Massachusetts. It becomes Bane a year later.

years.h: Backbone's singer takes the mic
years.p: Matt Firestone, first approached to sing, leaves after a few shows as Gateway. Aaron Bedard steps in, the band becomes Bane, and Zach Jordan joins on guitar.
years.xp: Bedard had sung for another Worcester hardcore band, Backbone. Wikipedia lists Jordan and Bedard as the core that played on until the 2016 farewell.

years.h: Five songs on tape in December
years.p: Bane record the demo with friends in the studio. Small releases around central Massachusetts follow.

years.h: Bane join the rest of Massachusetts hardcore on one compilation
years.p: Both Guns Blazing appears on They Came From Massachusetts, from Big Wheel Recreation.

years.h: Life Records puts out Forked Tongue
years.p: The EP is Bane's first proper release, after a year of shows across central Massachusetts.

yt: Full set at WPI, Worcester, April 5, 1997
years.h: Bellorado goes back to Converge after Free to Think, Free to Be
years.p: The second EP on Life Records comes out in early 1997. Ten Yard Fight's Ben Chused plays drums for about a year.

eras.title: Equal Vision and the first tours
eras.text: Equal Vision Records collected the early EPs on Holding This Moment, Bane toured the US for the first time, and by 2001 Brian McTernan was behind the board for Give Blood in Beltsville, Maryland.

yt: Full set at The Space, Worcester, October 23, 1998
years.h: Equal Vision gathers the early EPs, and Bane hit the road
years.p: Holding This Moment collects the earlier material on 7" and CD. The first US tour follows, with 19-year-old Nick Branigan of Close Call on drums.
years.xp: Ben Chused of Ten Yard Fight had held the drum seat since Damon Bellorado left to focus on Converge in 1997. Branigan took it in mid-1998 and kept it until 2003.

yt: Full set upstairs at the Palladium, Worcester, October 30, 1999
years.h: It All Comes Down to This gets made in Clinton, Massachusetts
years.p: Bane record their first full-length at Austin Enterprises in June 1999, and Equal Vision releases it.

years.cap: Flyer for Bane, Countervail, Jonny X and the Groadies and Life's End at The Schoolhouse, March 16, 1999
yt: Full set at the Palladium, Worcester, February 5, 2000
years.h: North America with Death by Stereo, then Europe for the first time
years.p: Adamantium is on the bill too. Bane also cover [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]]'s Just How Much for the compilation All Systems Go!.

years.h: Converge's Kurt Ballou produces Bane's side of the Adamantium split
years.p: The session is in early September 2000. Indecision Records puts the 7" out in 2001.

years.h: Give Blood comes out on Halloween
years.p: Brian McTernan records it in Beltsville, Maryland, that August. It runs 25 minutes and 40 seconds.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the record focuses on the hardcore scene, with themes of dreams and loss. Lambgoat gave it 9 out of 10.

Bane had claimed straight edge on an early release, but it was never their main subject. The original members stayed straight edge; Bob Mahoney and Stu Maguire did not. They still play the early straight-edge song Count Me Out.

eras.title: Bob Mahoney takes the sticks
eras.text: Mahoney replaced Nick Branigan on drums in 2003 and Bane played two weeks in Japan the next April. The Note, again with McTernan, came out in 2005, and bassist Pete Chilton left in 2007.

years.h: Bob Mahoney becomes Bane's fourth drummer
years.p: Nick Branigan leaves after five years and a US tour follows the change. Mahoney stays until the end and comes back for every reunion.

years.h: Bane spend two weeks touring Japan
years.p: The April 2004 tour is one of the band's first long runs overseas.

years.h: Comeback Kid and With Honor share the bill on a US run
years.p: The tour runs through March 2005, with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]] and With Honor.

years.h: The Note is made at Salad Days with McTernan again
years.p: Bane's third album comes out on Equal Vision in 2005, after sessions at Brian McTernan's Salad Days Studios.
years.xp: Wikipedia reads Wasted On The Young as possibly aimed at people who claim straight edge too early.

years.cap: Aaron Bedard at the Palladium, Worcester, December 30, 2006
years.h: Ten years in, Equal Vision issues an anniversary EP
years.p: The Ten Years Plus E.P. follows The Note on the label.

years.h: Pete Chilton, Bane's bassist since the start, leaves
years.p: Bane also record [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]]'s We Stand Alone for the tribute Our Impact Will Be Felt.

eras.title: Live from everywhere
eras.text: Stu Maguire took over on bass in 2008 and Bane put out three live albums in 2009, each named for a city and a clock time. Maguire left in 2012; by December 2013 the band was recording again.

years.h: Stu Maguire takes over on bass
years.p: He's known from Boston's Reach the Sky and has worked for the [[Dropkick Murphys|e8374874-4178-4869-b92e-fef6bf30dc04]] and [[The Mighty Mighty Bosstones|779353f3-6401-4cda-a8a2-6fd3ec9bc11b]].
years.xp: His family's account adds jobs at House of Blues, The Orpheum and the Pavilion for Live Nation.

years.cap: Bane live in Buenos Aires, June 22, 2008
years.h: Bane's 2009 live albums keep changing cities
years.p: Tokyo 7:58am (Alliance), Boston 6:58pm (Triple-B) and Los Angeles 3:58pm (6131) all come out in 2009. Overseas, some reappear as Perth, Curitiba, Dublin and Rome.
years.xp: Wikipedia's discography has Tokyo 7:58am also released as Perth 7:58am and Curitiba 7:58pm, Boston 6:58pm as Dublin 11:58pm, and Los Angeles 3:58pm as Rome 12:58am.

years.h: Chris Linkovich takes the bass as Stu Maguire leaves
years.p: Linkovich plays through 2014. Bane also cut Satan's Son for Triple-B's America's Hardcore Volume 2.

years.cap: Zach Jordan at Hellfest, Clisson, France, June 21, 2013
years.h: Bane head into the studio one more time
years.p: Alternative Press reports in December 2013 that recording has started, and that the band calls it their last album.

eras.title: The two-year goodbye
eras.text: In 2014 Bane called Don't Wait Up their last album and kept touring. The farewell ran to 2016, with a last show at the Worcester Palladium on June 18.

years.h: Bane call Don't Wait Up their last album, then keep touring
years.p: Alternative Press premieres the record in May 2014. James Siboni joins on bass.

years.h: The farewell tour reaches Webster Hall in New York
years.p: The date is May 8, 2016. IDIOTEQ later calls it the band's final concert, a month before Worcester.

years.cap: Bane's final show at the Palladium, Worcester, June 18, 2016
yt: hate5six: the final Worcester show, June 18, 2016
years.h: The last show is in Worcester, where Gateway began
years.p: Bane play the Palladium on June 18, 2016, with [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]] and The Promise on the bill, per Lambgoat.
years.xp: The farewell ran two years after Don't Wait Up. Wikipedia dates the last show to June 18, which is a month after the Webster Hall date IDIOTEQ gives. hate5six filmed the night.

eras.title: For Stu, and then for good
eras.text: Stu Maguire was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2019 and died in June 2021. Bane played his benefit that July, and in 2023 they booked Boston.

years.big: "Our beautiful bass player ... has found out that he has pancreatic cancer and that it has spread to his liver."
years.h: Stu Maguire learns he has pancreatic cancer
years.p: Bane's statement comes in January 2020. Maguire is in his early 40s, and his family sells merch to cover treatment while the band asks fans to buy it, write to him or share the campaign.
years.xp:
The shirts went on sale at imwithstu.limitedrun.com, with proceeds going to medical costs and family support.

IDIOTEQ's post says he was in aggressive chemotherapy every two weeks at Massachusetts General Hospital, with acupuncture and reiki alongside.

years.h: Pancreatic cancer takes Stu Maguire
years.p: Brendan "Stu" Maguire dies on June 27, 2021, a little under two years after his diagnosis.

years.h: Bane turn up unannounced at Stu Maguire's benefit
years.p: The surprise set comes five days after his death, at a benefit with [[The Bouncing Souls|429d5f26-329c-41cc-bdff-17c29dbf1fb8]], [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]], [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]] and Rebuilder.

years.big: "We missed this too much. We missed you too much."
years.src: IDIOTEQ: Bane is back · Wikipedia: Bane
years.h: Bane book Roadrunner in Boston for June 17
years.p: The announcement lands in the early hours of February 7, 2023, after a social media countdown that spelled out the band's name. [[The Suicide File|86336490-e9fb-41e3-9a81-8edfa56785ec]], [[Stick to Your Guns|07ef6bdd-20c8-4f2b-ac87-463f65b90768]] and [[Modern Life Is War|1bfdbf9d-e241-4ad7-8283-a3a7904bb6ca]] are on the bill.
years.xp: The show is all ages with no barricade. IDIOTEQ bills it as a one-time performance and lists Bracewar and Colin of Arabia as well; Wikipedia describes a two-night event at Roadrunner.
